recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is for FHIR-core. If OO wants to revisit SupplyRequest notDoneReason, refill/frequency semantics, or SupplyDelivery non-administration reasons, track that follow-up in the OO Incubator rather than editing inactive FHIR-core resource directories.
issue_request: FHIR-15945 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked OO to clarify blood product ordering and administration, including whether BiologicallyDerivedProduct, SupplyRequest, SupplyDelivery, and a statement-like resource should represent product, order, delivery/receipt, administration, and reasons for non-compliance. It also asked SupplyRequest to align better with request resources through intent, notDoneReason, refill/frequency, and clearer category/item semantics. The recorded resolution was to connect the balloter with the active OO project to ensure those use cases were covered.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentions FHIR-15945. The issue appears to have been applied through later healthcare-product work: SupplyRequest/DeviceRequest boundary changes clarified that SupplyRequest is inventory-oriented, FHIR-45453 added SupplyRequest.intent, and commit 71fdef0f0c introduced the Biologically Derived Product module with a ServiceRequest, BiologicallyDerivedProduct, SupplyDelivery, BiologicallyDerivedProductDispense, and Procedure workflow for BDP clinical use and blood transfusion examples.
additional_context: The current active resource list in source/fhir.ini includes BiologicallyDerivedProduct but no longer includes SupplyRequest, SupplyDelivery, or BiologicallyDerivedProductDispense. Commit 3b38b80cf2 removed those OO resources from FHIR-core and repointed BDP module links to the OO Incubator IG. Current in-scope core guidance links to the external SupplyDelivery and BDPDispense artifacts and uses ServiceRequest for clinical BDP requests. 2019 OO healthcare-product minutes also distinguish inventory supply flow from BDP matching/clinical use.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The remaining SupplyRequest and SupplyDelivery element questions are external to the current FHIR-core build; the active core BDP module already gives implementers the current recommended model and points to OO Incubator artifacts for the moved resources.

related_jiras.note: Clarified that SupplyRequest is for inventory management rather than patient-focused clinical requests, reinforcing the later ServiceRequest-centered BDP model.
Added SupplyRequest.intent using the request-intent pattern, covering one original SupplyRequest alignment concern before SupplyRequest moved out of core.
BDP stock distribution via SupplyDelivery was already represented on the combined branch by an external-repo audit commit.
SupplyDelivery changes were already represented on the combined branch by an external-repo audit commit after the OO Incubator move.
